Subject: Re: Capacity quote + OEM lead times for RWD-4657

Thanks Julien — useful detail. I pulled procurement + infra leads into thread to propose an actionable playbook we can run this quarter.

Proposal: "Sprint-to-seat" procurement staging playbook (high-level):
1) Immediate: commit a 20% buffer tranche (PO + deposit) to secure factory slot and avoid full-queue rebooking.
2) Week 0–8: provision cloud reserved capacity (Vertex) for onramp and initial QA. Cloud reservation should mirror the first tranche capacity requirements.
3) Week 8–12: first physical tranche delivery (targeted NVX-40G / NVX-48G mix) into staging pool; use prefix/KV cache warmup for canary customers.
4) Week 12–16+: remaining OEM deliveries; staggered onboarding and canary expansion.
5) Fallback: if OEM misses tranche, shift additional load to cloud burst and enable aggressive caching + lower-batch sizes to hold latency SLOs.
6) Governance: procurement milestone gating tied to invoice, Docusign acceptance, and a contingency credit clause from vendor.

I'm attaching a short staging-capacity-matrix.csv that maps tranche sizes to expected throughput and suggested canary cohorts. Also linking the procurement playbook draft in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xProcurePlaybook

Asks:
- Ben: can you confirm the minimal tranche size that keeps the Dedicated offering economically viable for the earliest customers?
- Karthik: can procurement accept 20% buffer PO terms (partial deposit now, remainder on shipment)?
- Julien / NovaHW: can you confirm willingness to commit an initial tranche and a tentative tranche release schedule?

On quoting: include the attached vendor_quote_v2.pdf in the procurement packet and we’ll request a stamped acknowledgement for tranche windows.

Thanks — I think a hybrid path here gives us the fastest safe onramp and keeps customer experience intact if OEM slippage occurs.

Regards,

Soojin Lee
Head of Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference
